title: Parliament SOC orders full loss assessment on 19 substandard coal shipments
author: Unknown
summary: Earlier estimate put losses from nine shipments at Rs. 8.5 bOfficials told to quantify total losses, including wear and tear at LakvijayaSouth African supplier fined $ 36.5 m over substandard coalMarrikkar flags delays in fresh procurement as existing stocks expected to run out by mid-September
content:
Earlier estimate put losses from nine shipments at Rs. 8.5 bOfficials told to quantify total losses, including wear and tear at LakvijayaSouth African supplier fined $ 36.5 m over substandard coalMarrikkar flags delays in fresh procurement as existing stocks expected to run out by mid-September

Parliament’s Sectoral Oversight Committee on Infrastructure and Strategic Development on Wednesday ordered a comprehensive assessment of losses caused by 19 shipments of substandard coal supplied to Sri Lanka between January and July, widening the scope of an earlier estimate that put losses from nine shipments at Rs.8.5 billion.Committee Chairman SJB MP S.M. Marrikkar this week said all 19 shipments received from the same South African supplier during the seven-month period had been found to be substandard. In March, Marrikkar disclosed that losses from nine shipments of substandard coal supplied by the company had amounted to Rs.8.5 billion.The Committee has now instructed officials from the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka, Lanka Coal Company, National System Operator and Lakvijaya Power Plant to form a committee headed by the Energy Ministry Secretary and prepare a comprehensive report quantifying the total losses.The assessment is also expected to account for wear and tear caused to the Lakvijaya Power Plant from the use of substandard coal.The Committee was informed that the South African supplier had been fined $ 36.5 million in penalties for the substandard coal, while an additional $ 611,000 had been invoiced as penalties for delayed deliveries.Marrikkar also raised concerns over delays in obtaining Cabinet approval to call fresh tenders for coal required from October, with existing stocks expected to be exhausted by mid-September.He urged the Energy Ministry Secretary to press the Minister to expedite the approval process to avoid delays in securing the next coal requirement.

title: Asahi Dyes and Chemicals opens  $ 20.4 m Biyagama manufacturing plant
author: Unknown
summary: President’s Special Envoy for Foreign Investment Hanif Yusoof and BOI Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa (second and third from left) open the new Asahi Dyes and Chemicals’ facility
content:
President’s Special Envoy for Foreign Investment Hanif Yusoof and BOI Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa (second and third from left) open the new Asahi Dyes and Chemicals’ facility

Japanese sustainable tech excellence, Italian innovation and Sri Lankan industrial capability uniteRepresents high-technology, environmentally sustainable and export-oriented investment

Sri Lanka’s high-value manufacturing and export sector received a significant boost yesterday with the official opening of the $ 20.4 million state-of-the-art manufacturing facility of Asahi Dyes and Chemicals SL   Ltd. at the Biyagama Export Processing Zone (BEPZ).Developed through a strategic partnership between Asahi Dyes and Chemicals Co., Ltd., of Japan and Asons Ltd., of Sri Lanka, the project represents a $ 20.4 million foreign direct investment, creating 281 direct employment opportunities while introducing advanced manufacturing technologies, internationally recognised production standards and world-class industrial expertise to Sri Lanka.

Speaking at the opening, BOI Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa commended the investment and the commitment behind it, wishing the company well. “This facility that has been built here will contribute to and enhance the vertical integration of the garment industry.

He added: “As I have always said, a great deal is said about the need to diversify our export base — into electronics, manufacturing, telecommunications, and other sectors — and we do need to. But the garment industry remains the bird in the hand. It has contributed tremendously to the growth of our economy over the years. Starting some 30 to 40 years ago, it has evolved into a highly sophisticated, high-technology industry.“We have achieved vertical integration in fabric and accessories, and we want to see the full range of supply-chain capability that our industry has built, thanks to the commitment of the people within it, supported and strengthened further. Our task now is to see how we grow this from here,” the BOI Chairman said.Founded in 1932, Asahi Dyes and Chemicals Co., Ltd., has earned an international reputation as a leading manufacturer of specialty chemicals, with expertise spanning sulfur chemistry, pharmaceutical intermediates, electronic chemicals and high-performance textile dyes. Operating across Japan, China and Vietnam, the company’s investment in Sri Lanka marks an important milestone in transferring advanced Japanese manufacturing technology, engineering expertise and global quality standards to the country’s industrial sector.The Biyagama facility will manufacture a range of specialty chemicals, including textile dyes, printing chemicals and finishing chemicals for the textile and apparel sector, serving export markets across Asia and Southeast Asia and strengthening Sri Lanka’s export portfolio and regional supply-chain resilience.A distinguishing feature of the operation is its connection with Tonello of Italy, one of the world’s leading technology companies specialising in garment washing, dyeing, finishing and sustainable textile processing solutions, with more than 10,000 machines deployed worldwide. This collaboration connects the Sri Lankan facility to a broader international network of technological innovation and responsible manufacturing, ensuring the operation benefits from ongoing global knowledge exchange.Sustainability is central to the new complex, which has been developed to comply with LEED v4 BD+C (New Construction) green building standards. Its operations incorporate water conservation, energy optimisation, advanced wastewater treatment, carbon emission reduction, and environmentally responsible production systems aligned with ESG principles — complementing Tonello’s own emphasis on water-efficient, digitally optimised and resource-efficient manufacturing.For Sri Lanka’s textile and apparel industry, the investment is expected to deliver substantial long-term value by localising the production of internationally certified specialty chemicals, reducing dependence on imported chemical inputs, improving supply-chain efficiency, enhancing export competitiveness, facilitating technology transfer, and developing highly skilled Sri Lankan professionals through exposure to advanced Japanese manufacturing systems.The investment strongly aligns with the strategic vision of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI) to attract high-technology, environmentally sustainable and export-oriented investments that generate long-term economic value, strengthen Sri Lanka’s industrial base, and position the country as a competitive manufacturing hub within South Asia.Asahi Dyes and Chemicals SL represents more than a single foreign investment project. It symbolises the convergence of Japanese technological excellence, Italian innovation and Sri Lankan industrial capability, creating a platform for sustainable growth, advanced manufacturing and international competitiveness — and reinforcing Sri Lanka’s ambition to become one of Asia’s leading destinations for high-value foreign direct investment.

title: Consumer sentiment lifts for second month in July
author: Unknown
summary: Consumer sentiment lifted, though marginally, for a second consecutive month in July, offering an early indication of stabilisation after fluctuations during the first half of 2026, according to Prosoft Research and Insights.The Consumer Sentiment Index rose to 80 in July from 79 in June, marking its second successive monthly increase since May and the first gradual stabilisation over two consecutive months since January.Prosoft said the movement was aligned with the Colombo Consumer Price Index (CCPI), which remained unchanged at 208, indicating stabilisation in overall price levels.However, the research firm cautioned against drawing firm conclusions from the latest improvement, citing fluctuations in consumer sentiment over the past six months, persistent inflationary pressures and the potential impact of El Niño.It said further monitoring over the coming months would be necessary to determine whether the recent improvement develops into a sustained trend.The index remains below its recent peak of 90 recorded in September 2024, when President Anura Kumara Dissanayake took office. Its lowest reading was 56 in June 2022, at the height of the economic and political crisis.Prosoft Research and Insights conducts its Consumer Sentiment Survey monthly among a sample of 200 respondents.
